lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: Kirk Cousins has triumphant return as Vikings sack Jordan Love 8 times in 30-10 win over Packers
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: GREEN BAY, Wis.  -- — Kirk Cousins began his second stint with Minnesota by showing just how much of a difference he can make for the Vikings' offense.  Cousins threw two touchdown passes and Levi Drake Rodriguez had two sacks as the Vikings took down Jordan Love eight times in a 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.  Cousins went 21 of 31 for 207 yards with an interception just five days after rejoining the Vikings, who acquired him from the Las Vegas Raiders at Tuesday’s trade deadline.

injuryReport.name: Coleman Shelton
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report

injuryReport.name: Terrance Ferguson
injuryReport.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
factors: Coaching/beat report confirms player will not be activated from IR this week
injuryReport.beatComment: Ferguson initially seemed to be making good progress in his recovery from the ankle injury, as the Rams elected to open his 21-day evaluation window Nov. 4. However, Ferguson's activation from IR was delayed after he strained his hamstring shortly after he resumed working out, and he hasn't practiced in more than two weeks. Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve as well as the Rams had hoped and now will require a procedure. Los Angeles will have to proceed without two of its top pass catchers for the remainder of the season, as Puka Nacua recently underwent an MCL surgery that entails an estimated 4-to-5-month recovery timeline.

injuryReport.name: Steve Avila
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
injuryReport.beatComment: The Rams' left guard was injured in Week 9 against the Commanders and will miss a second straight game. Bill Murray or Justin Dedich (undisclosed) projects to start in Avila's place versus Green Bay.

injuryReport.name: Kobie Turner
factors: 21-day IR window open (Week 1 ramp); logged Full Participation (FP) on Thursday
Requires formal 53-man roster activation prior to weekly NFL transaction deadline
injuryReport.beatComment: The Rams opened Turner's 21-day practice window Saturday. The defensive lineman missed the Rams' last four games while on IR due to a groin injury he sustained in Week 6 against the Cardinals. Given his ability to participate in full Monday, there appears to be a good chance he will be activated ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers.

injuryReport.name: Justin Dedich
factors: 21-day IR window open (Week 1 ramp); logged Full Participation (FP) on Thursday
Requires formal 53-man roster activation prior to weekly NFL transaction deadline
injuryReport.beatComment: The offensive lineman had his 21-day practice window opened over the weekend and appears ready to return to action Wednesday against the Packers. With all three of Steve Avila (hamstring), Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and Dylan McMahon (knee) injured, Dedich could immediately see snaps on the interior of the Rams' offensive line.

injuryReport.name: Kam Curl
injuryReport.beatComment: Curl posted two limited practices after beginning the week as a nonparticipant. The 27-year-old has started all 10 games for the Rams this season, recording 48 tackles (28 solo) and three pass deflections.

injuryReport.name: Myles Garrett
injuryReport.beatComment: Garrett was limited in practice Sunday and Tuesday due to a knee injury, but it doesn't appear he will be impacted in Wednesday night's matchup against the Packers. The 30-year-old has three tackles (three solo), including 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble in three regular-season games in 2026.

injuryReport.name: Kyren Williams
injuryReport.beatComment: Listed as a limited participant on the Rams' initial Week 12 injury report posted Sunday, Williams quelled any concern about his status for Wednesday's game against the Packers by taking full reps a day later. Though his sore toe isn't expected to affect his workload, Williams nonetheless may find himself in a timeshare with Blake Corum, who has been the more productive option on the ground this season. Williams has totaled seven touchdowns and is averaging 4.4 yards per carry through 10 games, while Corum has scored six times and is averaging 5.3 yards per tote.

injuryReport.name: Joe Cardona
factors: Beat/podium consensus: on track to suit up
injuryReport.beatComment: The Rams' long snapper was injured last Sunday against Arizona, but should be good to go for Wednesday versus Green Bay.

injuryReport.name: Davis Allen
injuryReport.beatComment: With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

injuryReport.name: Colby Parkinson
injuryReport.beatComment: Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

injuryReport.name: Tyler Higbee
factors: Habitual Veteran Rest prior (Tyler Higbee maintenance schedule)
injuryReport.beatComment: Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

irReserve.name: Davante Adams
irReserve.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
factors: Season-ending Injured Reserve — ineligible to return this season
irReserve.beatComment: The Rams have seemingly discounted the possibility of Adams coming off IR for a Wednesday matchup with the Packers in Week 12, while a Week 13 return is more plausible but still sounds like a "long shot," according to Rapoport. Instead, the Rams' Week 14 game against the 49ers on Dec. 13 would appear to be the most realistic target for Adams' return, especially since Los Angeles will effectively have a "mini-bye" ahead of that contest following its Thursday night matchup with Kansas City on Dec. 3. Whenever he's reinstated from IR, Adams should be in store for heavy target shares in the Rams' remaining games after star wideout Puka Nacua (knee) underwent season-ending MCL surgery earlier this week.

irReserve.name: Puka Nacua
irReserve.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
factors: Season-ending Injured Reserve — ineligible to return this season
irReserve.beatComment: Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith as the current healthy wideouts on the team's 53-man roster ahead of next Wednesday's tilt versus the Packers. Nacua, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, is slated to become a free agent in March.

irReserve.name: Dylan McMahon
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: McMahon suffered a knee injury during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. The injury is severe enough for McMahon to require a stint on IR, so he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, with his next chance to play being Week 16 against the Seahawks on Christmas Day. With Coleman Shelton nursing a hamstring injury, the Rams may have to turn to other options like David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer to fill in at center for the time being.

coachingMatchup.headline: Matt LaFleur & DC Jonathan Gannon vs. HC Sean McVay, OC Nathan Scheelhaase & DC Chris Shula (Road Test)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Green Bay Packers's staff (Matt LaFleur, OC Adam Stenavich, DC Jonathan Gannon) against Los Angeles Rams (6-4)—testing both Green Bay's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Matt LaFleur and OC Adam Stenavich pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress Los Angeles Rams's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Los Angeles Rams's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Jonathan Gannon balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Green Bay sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to Los Angeles Rams's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: Road Test situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Jordan Love, Tucker Kraft & Matthew Golden vs. CB Josh Wallace & LB Byron Young
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: GB: #3 Pass Off (268.1 yds) · #13 Off. Scoring (+1.25) | LAR: #2 Pass Def (-3.73)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Jordan Love, Tucker Kraft & Matthew Golden attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Los Angeles Rams's #2 pass defense (-3.73). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Green Bay's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Jordan Love (#10) scanning Rams's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Byron Young widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Tucker Kraft (#85).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Lukas Van Ness, Karl Brooks & Devonte Wyatt vs. QB Matthew Stafford & OT Alaric Jackson
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: GB: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | LAR: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Lukas Van Ness, Karl Brooks & Devonte Wyatt lead Green Bay's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Los Angeles Rams's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Packers keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Lukas Van Ness (#90) draw chip help from Rams's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Karl Brooks (#94).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Evan Williams, Zaire Franklin & Xavier McKinney vs. WR Konata Mumpfield & QB Matthew Stafford
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: GB: #10 Pass Def (-0.80) | LAR: #8 Pass Off (252.4 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Evan Williams, Zaire Franklin & Xavier McKinney anchor Green Bay's #10 pass defense (-0.80) against WR Konata Mumpfield and Los Angeles Rams's #8 passing attack (252.4 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Rams into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Evan Williams (#33) at the top of routes against WR Konata Mumpfield: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Matthew Stafford's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Chris Brooks & Christian Watson vs. Rams Front Seven & LB Byron Young
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: GB: #32 Rush Off (67.0 yds) | LAR: #6 Rush Def (-1.65)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Chris Brooks & Christian Watson test Los Angeles Rams's #6 run defense (-1.65) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Rams's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Rams's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Chris Brooks (#30).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Travis Glover, Jordan Morgan & Laken Tomlinson vs. DE Braden Fiske & Rams Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: GB: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | LAR: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Travis Glover, Jordan Morgan & Laken Tomlinson protect Jordan Love (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DE Braden Fiske and Los Angeles Rams's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Travis Glover (#79) on obvious passing downs—if DE Braden Fiske cannot win clean around the arc, Rams must dial up interior stunts that stress Jordan Morgan (#77).
